label: early original-phase h/u/v input (positions 1-3)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase, at positions 1-3; t=2 alone holds 58% of the mass. It never fires at t=0 or in the copy phase, and only trivially at <DEL>. The input token matters most: h (12x lift, 49% of mass), then u and v, with weaker tails on e, n and i. The strongest activations are h at t=1-2, and the top examples are mostly sequences starting with k (e.g. k i h, k w i h). Activation is lower when digits came earlier, and repeated tokens fire less than first occurrences. The predicate captures 84% of activation mass but has only about 33% precision. Many h/u/v steps at t=1-3 stay silent, depending on preceding tokens in a way that a prev_tok set raises only to about 0.5 F1. Lower-rate e/n/i activations are missed.
